slides.subtitle: Cost-reduction and data-product choices from the RMS estate census, tenant confidential
slides.title: Savings lie in object stores, not databases; products wait on rights

scqa: The census read 20 holding 1006. Of these, 638 were measured (63.4% of tables), and the estate holds 351.3 of data and index.

Databases are the smaller prize: only 15.2 (4.3%) looks reclaimable there, while all cost strategies together address 50,799.8 GiB. Quality is weak, with 23.0% of rows degraded, 81.7% with empty required-looking fields and 1.5% exact duplicates.
Which cost strategies and data-product candidates should be taken forward, and which deferred?

Take forward the archive-class move and the duplicate-object reconciliation, both as proposals to verify first. They carry most of the priced saving of 1,174.4 USD a month at list prices. Defer the small database strategies and all 8 until rights are granted and personal data is removed.

slides.title: Two object-store strategies account for almost all reclaimable bytes

points: The estate comprises 20 and 1006. Only 638 were measured, which is 63.4% of tables; remaining ratios rest on stratified samples.
Data and index held total 351.3. The largest databases account for 350.3 GiB, a share of 99.7%.
Before pricing, 15.2 looks reclaimable inside databases, which is 4.3% of database bytes.
368 are empty by row estimate, though a freshly truncated live table looks the same.
slides.title: The census covers the whole estate but measured only part of the tables

points: Exact duplicate rows are 1.5% of rows, so de-duplication inside tables offers little.
Degraded rows are 23.0% of rows, a material defect for any analytical or licensed product.
Rows with empty required-looking fields are 81.7%. This is a heuristic, so treat it as a signal, not a verdict.
Personal-data markers appear in 71.8% of sampled rows. The detector is sampled, so absence of a marker is not absence of personal data.
slides.title: Quality and personal-data exposure, not duplication, limit what the data can be used for

points: Personal-data markers were sampled from 1.0m rows, so the marker rate rests on a sample, not a full pass.
Bytes not written for over a year are 15.4% of the total, a measured and sizeable share of potentially archivable data.
The estate holds 259.3m rows, an estimate, so row-based product sizing is indicative only.
71 of duplicate table pairs exist, but copies may be deliberate staging or backups; confirm ownership before retirement.

slides.title: The three priced strategies differ widely in bytes, monthly saving and confidence

points: Confirm read frequency and retrieval fees for the archive move: 42,891.0 GiB, worth 986.5 USD monthly.
Confirm duplicate objects by content before deleting; 7,839.5 GiB is a size-based estimate worth 180.3 USD monthly.
Defer database cold storage; 5.9 USD monthly does not justify early effort.
Hold all 8 at specification stage until rights are bound and personal data is removed.

points: Only 638 of 1006 were measured, so sampled ratios are estimates; a complete-pass census would close this.

The artists_app connection is unread and some buckets are unreachable; a read grant and reconciled bucket inventory would close this.
